# Text tasks
![](images/text_task.png){style="width:150px; background:white; border-radius:5px; border: white solid 5px" fig-align="center"}

To familiarise yourself with the text outputs of `maaslin3()` please attempt the below tasks.
This involves answering some MCQs (multiple choice questions) and creating some of your own code.

## Significant results

Please attempt the below MCQs based on the significant results table.

You can find the results by searching through the HTML we created earlier (`significant_results.html`).
The instructions on how to use the html file are here: [Explore HTML table](/maaslin3/html_table.qmd#explore-html-table).

You can also find the answers using various [`tidyverse` functions](https://neof-workshops.github.io/Tidyverse/) on the `sig_res_tbl` object.

### Arranging questions
![](images/question_bubble_ibm_orange.png){style="width:150px; background:white; border-radius:5px; border: white solid 5px" fig-align="center"}

The first three questions can be carried out by ordering the specific columns by clicking on the column name in the HTML.
Optionally, [`dplyr::slice()` functions](https://neof-workshops.github.io/Tidyverse/dplyr/slice.html) and the [`dplyr::pull()` function](https://neof-workshops.github.io/Tidyverse/dplyr/pull.html) can be used.

```{r, echo = FALSE}
opts_p <- c(
    answer="*Leifsonia*",
    "*Oligoflexus*", 
    "*Terrimonas*")
```
1. Which feature/genus has the most significant q-value for one of its associations? `r longmcq(opts_p)`

```{r, echo = FALSE}
opts_p <- c(
    "*Leifsonia*",
    "*Oligoflexus*", 
    answer="*Terrimonas*")
```
2. Which feature/genus has the largest coefficient value? `r longmcq(opts_p)`

```{r, echo = FALSE}
opts_p <- c(
    "*Leifsonia*",
    answer="*Oligoflexus*",
    "*Terrimonas*")
```
3. Which feature/genus has the lowest `N_not_zero` value? `r longmcq(opts_p)`

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="MCQ1 code"}
```{r, eval=FALSE}
#MCQ1
#Feature with most significant q-value
sig_res_tbl |>
    dplyr::slice_min(qval_individual, n=1) |>
    dplyr::pull(feature)
```
:::
::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="MCQ2 code"}
```{r, eval=FALSE}
#MCQ2
#Feature with largest coefficient value
sig_res_tbl |>
    dplyr::slice_max(coef, n=1) |>
    dplyr::pull(feature)
```
:::
::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="MCQ3 code"}
```{r, eval=FALSE}
#MCQ3
#Feature with lowest N_not_zero
sig_res_tbl |>
    dplyr::slice_min(N_not_zero, n=1) |>
    dplyr::pull(feature)
```
:::

### Specific comparisons questions
![](images/question_bubble_ibm_purple.png){style="width:150px; background:white; border-radius:5px; border: white solid 5px" fig-align="center"}

The next three question involve looking up the results of a specific feature and association.
This can be carried out with the search bar in the HTML.
With tidyverse you can use multiple [`dplyr::filter()` functions](https://neof-workshops.github.io/Tidyverse/dplyr/filter.html) and the [`dplyr::pull()` function](https://neof-workshops.github.io/Tidyverse/dplyr/pull.html).

```{r, echo = FALSE}
opts_p <- c(
    answer="**-3.01210265002215**", 
    "**2.36040830013277**", 
    "**3.3300534208379**")
```
4. What is the coefficient value of *Kribella* for the Rhizosphere Soil vs Bulk Soil comparison for the abundance model? `r longmcq(opts_p)`

```{r, echo = FALSE}
opts_p <- c(
    "**-3.01210265002215**", 
    "**2.36040830013277**", 
    answer="**3.3300534208379**")
```
5. What is the coefficient value of *Bordetella* for the Rhizosphere Soil vs Bulk Soil comparison for the prevalence model? `r longmcq(opts_p)`

```{r, echo = FALSE}
opts_p <- c(
    "**-3.01210265002215**", 
    answer="**2.36040830013277**", 
    "**3.3300534208379**")
```
6. What is the coefficient value of *Azospira* for the reads association for the prevalence model? `r longmcq(opts_p)`

`r hide("MCQ4 code")`
```{r, eval=FALSE}
#MCQ4
#Coefficient value of Kribbella for Soil comparison
# for the abundance model
sig_res_tbl |>
    dplyr::filter(feature=="Kribbella") |>
    dplyr::filter(name=="SoilRhizosphere Soil") |>
    dplyr::filter(model=="abundance") |>
    dplyr::pull(coef)
```
`r unhide()`
`r hide("MCQ5 code")`
```{r, eval=FALSE}
#MCQ5
#Coefficient value of Bordetella for Soil comparison
# for the prevalence model
sig_res_tbl |>
    dplyr::filter(feature=="Bordetella") |>
    dplyr::filter(name=="SoilRhizosphere Soil") |>
    dplyr::filter(model=="prevalence") |>
    dplyr::pull(coef)
```
`r unhide()`
`r hide("MCQ6 code")`
```{r, eval=FALSE}
#MCQ6
#Coefficient value of Azospira for Reads association
# for the prevalence model
sig_res_tbl |>
    dplyr::filter(feature=="Azospira") |>
    dplyr::filter(name=="Reads") |>
    dplyr::filter(model=="prevalence") |>
    dplyr::pull(coef)
```
`r unhide()`

## All results
![](images/question_bubble_ibm_yellow.png){style="width:150px; background:white; border-radius:5px; border: white solid 5px" fig-align="center"}

For this task you will read in the all results file as a tibble.

- File to read in: `genu_output/all_results.tsv`
- Output tibble name: `all_res_tbl`
- Glimpse the tibble once it is created
- Create a HTML table file with the contents of `all_res_tbl`
- Use the instructions for the significant results as a guide: [sig results page](/maaslin3/html_table.qmd)
- Feel free to copy and paste your previous code but ensure you edit/change the relevant names

Answer the below MCQs based on the `sig_res_tbl` and `all_res_tbl` objects.

```{r, echo = FALSE}
opts_p <- c(
    "**15**", 
    answer="**689**", 
    "**1,404**")
```
1. How many observations are there in the significant results table? `r longmcq(opts_p)`

```{r, echo = FALSE}
opts_p <- c(
    "**15**", 
    "**689**", 
    answer="**1,404**")
```
2. How many observations are there in the all results table? `r longmcq(opts_p)`

`r hide("Read in tibble solution")`
```{r, eval=FALSE}
#Read in all results
all_res_tbl <- readr::read_delim(
    file = "./genus_output/all_results.tsv", 
    delim="\t")
all_res_tbl |> glimpse()
```
`r unhide()`

`r hide("HTML table solution")`
```{r, eval=FALSE}
#Create HTML object
all_res_dt <- DT::datatable(all_res_tbl, options = list(pageLength = 20))
#Save HTML
htmlwidgets::saveWidget(
    #Input widget/html
    widget = all_res_dt,
    #Output html
    file = "./genus_output/all_results.html",
    #Save as a single self contained HTML
    selfcontained = TRUE)

```
`r unhide()`


::: {.callout-note title="Table too big"}
In your future research you may have a table that is too big to convert to a HTML with `DT::datatable()`.
If this is the case you'll get the following warning:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
Warning message in instance$preRenderHook(instance):
“It seems your data is too big for client-side DataTables. You may consider server-side processing: https://rstudio.github.io/DT/server.html”
```

Unfortunately the link in the suggestion is dead.
Most likely trying to setup server-side processing will be incredibly difficult and not worth the effort to view all the results as an HTML.
Therefore, you'll need to look at the table through an R `tibble` or possibly through excel.
:::
